question.:question/problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-6y &=-8 \\ -4x+24y &=32.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then find the general solution of the linear system.
question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we set up the augmented matrix for the system:

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & -6 & -8 \\ -4 & 24 & 32\end{array}\right]
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & -6 & -8 \\ -4 & 24 & 32\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+4{R}_{1} \\  & \sim\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & -6 & -8 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{array}\right].\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-6y &=-8 \\ 0x+0y &=0.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Since any pair of numbers $x,y$ is a solution of the final equation $0x+0y=0,$ we can remove this equation from the system. So, our system now consists of a single equation

$$
x-6y=-8.
$$

The first variable $(x)$ is the basic variable, and the second variable $(y)$ is the free variable. Solving for the basic variable $(x)$ in terms of the free variable $(y),$ we get $x=6y-8,$ and the general solution is

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x &=6y-8 \\ y &=y\end{aligned}\right.
$$

where $y$ is an arbitrary number.

In vector form, the general solution can be written as

$$
\begin{bmatrix}x \\ y\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}6y-8 \\ y\end{bmatrix},\,y\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$
